summary: Hermann Kulke earned his PhD from the University of Freiburg and worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held the Chair of Asian History at the University of Kiel from 1988 and had an attested post at Heidelberg University in 2004.

Hermann Oldenberg studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1871-1875) before working in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Berlin (~1878-1889), the University of Kiel (~1889-1904), and the University of Göttingen (~1904-1920).

Hermann Osthoff worked in linguistics and Indology, founding Morphologische Untersuchungen auf dem Gebiete der indogermanischen Sprachen. He held academic posts at Leipzig University (~1875-1877) and Heidelberg University (~1877-1909).

Hermann Sauppe was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Zurich from approximately 1838 to 1845 and at the University of Göttingen from approximately 1856 to 1893.

Hermann Wilhelm Ebel studied linguistics at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1836-1840) and the University of Halle-Wittenberg under August Friedrich Pott (~1840-1842). He later held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from approximately 1872 to 1875.

Hermann von Schlagintweit studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1845-1848). A scholar in history, archaeology, and other fields, he held a post at Humboldt University of Berlin from approximately 1851 to 1854.
Hideaki Kimura completed doctoral studies at Taisho University in Buddhist studies and Indology. He later held a research post at Taisho University, attested in 1995.

Hideaki Nakatani studied at Kyoto University under Gadjin Nagao, trained under Yutaka Ochihara, and earned a PhD from Sorbonne Nouvelle University. In Indology and Buddhist studies, he was attested as a professor at Kobe Gakuin University in 2003.
Hidehiko Kurita earned a PhD from Tohoku University and works in religious studies and Japanology. He held a lecturer post attested at Aichi Prefectural University in 2020.
Hideki Kiyoshima studied at the University of Delhi, working in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held an attested lecturer post at Kindai University in 1989.

Hidenaka Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo from approximately 1906 to 1909. Working in linguistics, history, and archaeology, he held an academic post at Kyoto Women's University from around 1949 to 1958.

Sakuma studied at the University of Tokyo and earned a PhD under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg. Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, he held posts at Shitennoji University, Taisho University, and the University of Tsukuba.

Hideo Mineshima studied at Taisho University and worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He was a professor at Waseda University (~1970-1998, attested 1999) and held posts at Bunkyo Gakuin University (~1998-2003) and Sanko Research Institute (attested 2008).
Hideo Sakurai studied at Tohoku University from approximately 1940 to 1943. A scholar of Buddhist studies, he held an attested post as professor emeritus at Komazawa University between 1982 and 1992.

Hideomi Yaita completed doctoral studies at Taisho University in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held research assistant posts at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1991, 1995) and a lecturer post at Taisho University (attested 1995).
Hideto Ono studied at Komazawa University and worked in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He held an assistant professor post at Aichi Gakuin University from approximately 1985 to 1995.
Hidetoshi Yoshizawa is a scholar in Buddhist studies who held posts at Taisho University as a researcher (attested 1998-2008) and chief research fellow (attested 2017).

Hideyo Ogawa studied at Hiroshima University (~1973-1982) and worked in Indology and philosophy. He held posts there as assistant professor (~1990-1997) and professor in the Department of Indian Philosophy, Graduate School of Letters (~1997-2019).
Hideyuki Matsumori was a doctoral student at Soka University (attested 2006) and held an assistant professor post there in Buddhist studies and Indology (attested 2015).
Hildegard Diemberger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies who completed supervised work under Luciano Petech and Ernst Steinkellner.
